title: UPDATE: Global Pension Funds Cut US Stocks Over AI Risk Concerns
summary:
The Financial Times reports that institutional investors are divesting from American equities because of perceived dangers in the artificial intelligence sector. This trend follows a wave of selling by pension funds throughout September, suggesting that AI risk concerns are a primary driver behind the shift in asset allocation.

Goldman Sachs estimated that US pension funds would sell $33 billion in stocks around the end of September, a volume in the 98th percentile since 2000. A later analysis modeled a $30.5 billion sell-off, contributing to a $11.5 billion market-on-close sell imbalance. Systematic commodity trading advisors could offset these flows by buying between $11.5 billion and $30 billion if markets remain flat or rise, though they would likely sell $15.8 billion more if indices decline.

GOLDMAN: U.S. PENSION FUNDS SET TO SELL $33 BILLION IN STOCKS

Goldman Sachs estimates $33 billion in U.S. pension fund equity selling around September month-end, a flow ranking in the 98th percentile since 2000.

Meanwhile, systematic CTAs could provide an offset, buying $11.5 billion globally in flat markets or nearly $30 billion if stocks rise.

If markets fall, however, CTAs could flip to $15.8 billion in additional selling.
